claim: Canine distemper virus (CDV) belongs to morbillivirus, including measles virus (MeV) and rinderpest virus.
source: Canine distemper virus (CDV) belongs to morbillivirus, including measles virus (MeV) and rinderpest virus, which causes serious immunological and neurological disorders in carnivores, including dogs and rhesus monkeys, as recently reported, but their vaccines are highly effective.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a classification statement.

claim: CDV causes serious immunological and neurological disorders in carnivores, including dogs and rhesus monkeys.
source: Canine distemper virus (CDV) belongs to morbillivirus, including measles virus (MeV) and rinderpest virus, which causes serious immunological and neurological disorders in carnivores, including dogs and rhesus monkeys, as recently reported, but their vaccines are highly effective.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract with reference to recent reports.

claim: CDV vaccines are highly effective.
source: Canine distemper virus (CDV) belongs to morbillivirus, including measles virus (MeV) and rinderpest virus, which causes serious immunological and neurological disorders in carnivores, including dogs and rhesus monkeys, as recently reported, but their vaccines are highly effective.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract.

claim: The attachment glycoprotein hemagglutinin (CDV-H) at the CDV surface utilizes signaling lymphocyte activation molecule (SLAM) and Nectin-4 as entry receptors.
source: The attachment glycoprotein hemagglutinin (CDV-H) at the CDV surface utilizes signaling lymphocyte activation molecule (SLAM) and Nectin-4 (also called poliovirus-receptor-like-4; PVRL4) as entry receptors.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract.

claim: The crystal structure of the globular head domain of CDV-H vaccine strain was determined at 3.2 Å resolution.
source: Here, we determined the crystal structure of the globular head domain of CDV-H vaccine strain at 3.2 Å resolution, revealing that CDV-H exhibits a highly tilted homodimeric form with a six-bladed β-propeller fold.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a primary finding of the study.

claim: CDV-H exhibits a highly tilted homodimeric form with a six-bladed β-propeller fold.
source: Here, we determined the crystal structure of the globular head domain of CDV-H vaccine strain at 3.2 Å resolution, revealing that CDV-H exhibits a highly tilted homodimeric form with a six-bladed β-propeller fold.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a structural finding from the crystal structure.

claim: The predicted Nectin-4-binding site is well conserved with that of MeV-H.
source: While the predicted Nectin-4-binding site is well conserved with that of MeV-H, that of SLAM is similar but partially different, which is expected to contribute to host specificity.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract based on structural comparison.

claim: The SLAM-binding site of CDV-H is similar but partially different from that of MeV-H, which is expected to contribute to host specificity.
source: While the predicted Nectin-4-binding site is well conserved with that of MeV-H, that of SLAM is similar but partially different, which is expected to contribute to host specificity.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract with an inference about host specificity.

claim: Five N-linked sugars covered a broad area of the CDV-H surface to expose receptor-binding sites only.
source: Five N-linked sugars covered a broad area of the CDV-H surface to expose receptor-binding sites only, supporting the effective production of neutralizing antibodies.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a structural finding.

claim: The glycan shield of CDV-H supports the effective production of neutralizing antibodies.
source: Five N-linked sugars covered a broad area of the CDV-H surface to expose receptor-binding sites only, supporting the effective production of neutralizing antibodies.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an interpretation of the structural finding.

claim: The glycan shield features are common to MeV-H, although the glycosylation sites are completely different.
source: These features are common to MeV-H, although the glycosylation sites are completely different.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract comparing CDV-H and MeV-H.

claim: High-speed atomic force microscopy revealed highly mobile features of the CDV-H dimeric head via the connector region.
source: Furthermore, real-time observation using high-speed atomic force microscopy revealed highly mobile features of the CDV-H dimeric head via the connector region.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a finding from HS-AFM experiments.

claim: Sugar-shielded tilted homodimeric structure and dynamic conformational changes are common characteristics of morbilliviruses and ensure effective fusion entry and vaccination.
source: These results suggest that sugar-shielded tilted homodimeric structure and dynamic conformational changes are common characteristics of morbilliviruses and ensure effective fusion entry and vaccination.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a conclusion from the study.

claim: CDV infects dogs as well as other carnivores.
source: Canine distemper virus (CDV) infects dogs as well as other carnivores, and causes acute, highly contagious, febrile diseases that affect the respiratory, gastrointestinal, and central nervous systems, along with serious temporary immunodeficiency (Appel and Summers, 1995; An et al., 2008; von Messling et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: CDV causes acute, highly contagious, febrile diseases that affect the respiratory, gastrointestinal, and central nervous systems, along with serious temporary immunodeficiency.
source: Canine distemper virus (CDV) infects dogs as well as other carnivores, and causes acute, highly contagious, febrile diseases that affect the respiratory, gastrointestinal, and central nervous systems, along with serious temporary immunodeficiency (Appel and Summers, 1995; An et al., 2008; von Messling et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: In 2008, the Chinese group reported a natural infection of CDV in rhesus monkeys, indicating that the CDV expanded its host range.

claim: CDV is an enveloped virus with a non-segmented, negative-strand RNA genome.
source: CDV is an enveloped virus with a non-segmented, negative-strand RNA genome that is classified in the genus Morbillivirus of the family Paramyxoviridae, to which the measles virus (MeV) also belongs.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction as a classification statement.

claim: CDV is classified in the genus Morbillivirus of the family Paramyxoviridae.
source: CDV is an enveloped virus with a non-segmented, negative-strand RNA genome that is classified in the genus Morbillivirus of the family Paramyxoviridae, to which the measles virus (MeV) also belongs.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction as a classification statement.

claim: SLAM has two immunoglobulin (Ig)-like domains in the extracellular region.
source: SLAM, which has two immunoglobulin (Ig)-like domains in the extracellular region, is expressed on thymocytes, activated lymphocytes, mature dendritic cells, macrophages, and platelets, reflecting the tropism and immunosuppressive nature of CDV (Yanagi et al., 2009; Schwartzberg et al., 2009; Kiel et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: SLAM is expressed on thymocytes, activated lymphocytes, mature dendritic cells, macrophages, and platelets.
source: SLAM, which has two immunoglobulin (Ig)-like domains in the extracellular region, is expressed on thymocytes, activated lymphocytes, mature dendritic cells, macrophages, and platelets, reflecting the tropism and immunosuppressive nature of CDV (Yanagi et al., 2009; Schwartzberg et al., 2009; Kiel et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Nectin-4 has three Ig-like domains as an extracellular region.
source: On the other hand, Nectin-4 has three Ig-like domains as an extracellular region and is expressed on epithelial cells, permitting transmission from the basal to the apical side for the spread of viruses (Takeda et al., 2007; Tahara et al., 2008; Leonard et al., 2008; Mühlebach et al., 2011; Noyce et al., 2011; Noyce and Richardson, 2012).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Nectin-4 is expressed on epithelial cells, permitting transmission from the basal to the apical side for the spread of viruses.

evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The mechanism of viral infection is similar to that of MeV, while CDV tends to cause more serious neurological disruption.
source: The mechanism of viral infection is similar to that of MeV, while CDV tends to cause more serious neurological disruption.

claim: The host species of CDV is partly determined by their SLAMs.
source: Our recent report and other studies have demonstrated that the host species of CDV is partly determined by their SLAMs (Fukuhara et al., 2019; Ohishi et al., 2014), while the host innate immunity should also be considered (Takeda et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Some recent CDV strains can infect monkeys, such as rhesus and cynomolgus monkeys, raising the possibility of further expansion of host specificities.
source: Notably, some recent CDV strains can infect monkeys, such as rhesus and cynomolgus monkeys, raising the possibility of further expansion of host specificities (Qiu et al., 2011).

claim: Single amino acid substitutions (R519S, D540G, and P541S) can cause CDV-A75/17 or CYN07dV strains to infect Vero cells expressing human SLAM.
source: Single amino acid substitutions (R519S, D540G, and P541S) can cause CDV-A75/17 or CYN07dV strains to infect Vero cells expressing human SLAM (Sakai et al., 2013; Bieringer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The crystal structures of the H protein of MeV (MeV-H) revealed a six-bladed β-propeller folded head domain similar to those of Hemagglutinin/Neuraminidase (HN) proteins of the other paramyxoviruses.
source: The crystal structures of the H protein of MeV (MeV-H) revealed a six-bladed β-propeller folded head domain similar to those of Hemagglutinin/Neuraminidase (HN) proteins of the other paramyxoviruses.

claim: The MeV-H forms a disulfide-linked homodimer in unique tilted orientation.

claim: Live attenuated vaccines of CDV developed for more than half a century are highly effective.
source: Live attenuated vaccines of CDV developed for more than half a century are highly effective, while there are no officially available vaccines for other carnivores, such as lions, ferrets, and earless seals (Rouxel et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: There are no officially available vaccines for other carnivores, such as lions, ferrets, and earless seals.
source: Live attenuated vaccines of CDV developed for more than half a century are highly effective, while there are no officially available vaccines for other carnivores, such as lions, ferrets, and earless seals (Rouxel et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: MeV-H has sugar shields that cover a large surface, except for the binding sites of human SLAM and Nectin-4.
source: MeV-H has sugar shields that cover a large surface, except for the binding sites of human SLAM and Nectin-4.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction based on previous structural studies.

claim: The anti-MeV-H antibodies induced by vaccines tend to target the receptor-binding sites (RBSs), ensuring the efficient production of neutralizing antibodies.
source: The anti-MeV-H antibodies induced by vaccines tend to target the receptor-binding sites (RBSs), ensuring the efficient production of neutralizing antibodies (Hashiguchi et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: CDV-H protein can bind to dog SLAM with a μM range of Kd.
source: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) analyses in two previous reports showed that the CDV-H protein can bind to dog SLAM with a μM range of Kd (Fukuhara et al., 2019; Khosravi et al., 2016), but there has been no observation that CDV-H binds to the Nectin-4 ligand at the protein level.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with supporting citations.

claim: CDV-H binds to dNectin-4 with low affinity (Kd ~ 10−7 to 10−6 M) and fast kinetics.
source: SPR analysis revealed that CDV-H binds to dNectin-4 with low affinity (Kd ~ 10−7 to 10−6 M) and fast kinetics (Figure 1D ; Table 1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by SPR data shown in Figure 1D and Table 1.

claim: The binding characteristics of the CDV-H–dNectin-4 interaction were similar to those of CDV-H–SLAM.
source: The binding characteristics of the CDV-H–dNectin-4 interaction were similar to those of CDV-H–SLAM, which is typical for receptor recognition of viral attachment proteins.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section based on SPR analysis.

claim: CDV-H exhibits a sufficient response to hNectin-4 with similar binding kinetics to the CDV-H–dNectin-4 interaction.
source: SPR experiments clearly demonstrated that CDV-H exhibits a sufficient response to hNectin-4 with similar binding kinetics to the CDV-H–dNectin-4 interaction, as shown in Figure 1D and Table 1.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by SPR data shown in Figure 1D and Table 1.

claim: The molecular weight of the non-reducing soluble CDV-H determined by gel filtration chromatography and SDS–PAGE matched its dimer form.
source: The molecular weight of the non-reducing soluble CDV-H determined by gel filtration chromatography and sodium dodecyl sulfate–polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS–PAGE) matched its dimer form (Figure 1B), indicating that the head domain of CDV-H exists as a disulfide-linked homodimer.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The head domain of CDV-H exists as a disulfide-linked homodimer.
source: The molecular weight of the non-reducing soluble CDV-H determined by gel filtration chromatography and sodium dodecyl sulfate–polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS–PAGE) matched its dimer form (Figure 1B), indicating that the head domain of CDV-H exists as a disulfide-linked homodimer.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The crystal structure of CDV-H was refined at 3.2 Å resolution by molecular replacement using the MeV-H structure.
source: We determined the crystal structure of CDV-H refined at 3.2 Å resolution by molecular replacement using the MeV-H structure (Hashiguchi et al., 2007), which shares approximately 30% sequence identity in the head domain with CDV-H as a search probe (Figure 2B and Table 2).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2B and Table 2.

claim: MeV-H shares approximately 30% sequence identity in the head domain with CDV-H.
source: We determined the crystal structure of CDV-H refined at 3.2 Å resolution by molecular replacement using the MeV-H structure (Hashiguchi et al., 2007), which shares approximately 30% sequence identity in the head domain with CDV-H as a search probe (Figure 2B and Table 2).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

claim: There are two CDV-H monomers (chains A and B) in the asymmetric unit of the crystals, which have only slight differences (root mean square deviation = 0.301 Å) in the structures of some loops.
source: There are two CDV-H monomers (chains A and B) in the asymmetric unit of the crystals, which have only slight differences (root mean square deviation = 0.301 Å) in the structures of some loops (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The head domains of CDV-H of vaccine strain exhibit a six-bladed β-propeller structure, which is essentially the same as recent cryo-EM structure of wild-type CDV-H ectodomain (r.m.s.d. = 0.584–0.743 Å).
source: The head domains of CDV-H of vaccine strain exhibit a six-bladed β-propeller structure, which is essentially the same as recent cryo-EM structure of wild-type CDV-H ectodomain (r.m.s.d. = 0.584–0.743 Å) (Kalbermatter et al., 2023), similar to that of the MeV-H structures (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with a supporting citation and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: CDV-H forms a homodimer structure facing the β-propeller 2, α1 and α2 helices, resulting in a dimer orientation inclined to the horizontal plane.
source: Furthermore, CDV-H forms a homodimer structure facing the β-propeller 2, α1 and α2 helices, resulting in a dimer orientation inclined to the horizontal plane (Figure 3A), similar to the MeV-H homodimer structures and distinct from other paramyxoviruses, such as parainfluenza virus 5 (Figure 3B; Hashiguchi et al., 2007; Yin et al., 2006; Yuan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: The homodimer orientation of CDV-H is similar to the MeV-H homodimer structures and distinct from other paramyxoviruses, such as parainfluenza virus 5.
source: Furthermore, CDV-H forms a homodimer structure facing the β-propeller 2, α1 and α2 helices, resulting in a dimer orientation inclined to the horizontal plane (Figure 3A), similar to the MeV-H homodimer structures and distinct from other paramyxoviruses, such as parainfluenza virus 5 (Figure 3B; Hashiguchi et al., 2007; Yin et al., 2006; Yuan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with supporting citations and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The interactions at the homodimer interface are mainly composed of three parts: the top, middle, and bottom sections.
source: The interactions at the homodimer interface are mainly composed of three parts: the top, middle, and bottom sections, as shown in Figure 3A.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The top section of CDV-H is a hydrophobic cluster consisting of Leu201, Val203, Trp259, Leu260, and Leu265, which interact with Leu205, Leu209, Leu234, and Ile248, respectively.
source: The top section of CDV-H is a hydrophobic cluster consisting of Leu201, Val203, Trp259, Leu260, and Leu265, which interact with Leu205, Leu209, Leu234, and Ile248, respectively.

claim: The unique dimer orientation is a common feature of morbilliviruses and is appropriate for binding to the protein receptors SLAM and Nectin-4.
source: These findings suggest that the unique dimer orientation is a common feature of morbilliviruses and is appropriate for binding to the protein receptors SLAM and Nectin-4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).

claim: The superposition of the current CDV-H structure onto each individual complex structure enabled the construction of a reasonable CDV-H–receptor complex model without any significant structural hindrance.

claim: Eight amino acids (Tyr525, Asp526, Ile527, Ser528, Arg529, Tyr547, Thr548, and Arg552) on the β5 blade of CDV-H are important for interaction with dSLAM.
source: Previous mutagenesis studies have reported that eight amino acids (Tyr525, Asp526, Ile527, Ser528, Arg529, Tyr547, Thr548, and Arg552) on the β5 blade of CDV-H are important for interaction with dSLAM (von Messling et al., 2005; Zipperle et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with supporting citations.

claim: CDV-H binds to dSLAM in a manner similar to MeV-H–tamarin SLAM interaction.
source: Therefore, CDV-H binds to dSLAM in a manner similar to MeV-H–tamarin SLAM interaction.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section as a conclusion from structural comparison.

claim: 10 of the 24 interacting residues were identical in MeV-H with CDV-H.
source: To examine CDV-H binding to dog Nectin-4, the superposition of CDV-H onto the MeV-H–hNectin-4 complex structure (Zhang et al., 2013) revealed that 10 of the 24 interacting residues were identical in MeV-H with CDV-H, while all 20 interacting residues of hNectin-4 were identical to dNectin-4 (Figure 5B, C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claim: All 20 interacting residues of hNectin-4 were identical to dNectin-4.
source: To examine CDV-H binding to dog Nectin-4, the superposition of CDV-H onto the MeV-H–hNectin-4 complex structure (Zhang et al., 2013) revealed that 10 of the 24 interacting residues were identical in MeV-H with CDV-H, while all 20 interacting residues of hNectin-4 were identical to dNectin-4 (Figure 5B, C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claim: Both dNectin-4 and hNectin-4 could bind to CDV-H.
source: As mentioned above, SPR analysis demonstrated that both dNectin-4 and hNectin-4 could bind to CDV-H (Figure 1D).

claim: The binding mode of CDV-H to dNectin-4 is presumably the same as that of MeV-H to hNectin-4.
source: This result suggests that the binding mode of CDV-H to dNectin-4 is presumably the same as that of MeV-H to hNectin-4.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section as an inference from the structural and binding data.

claim: There were five potential glycosylation sites (Asn149, Asn391, Asn422, Asn456, and Asn587) in the H protein head domain of the Kyoto Biken vaccine strain (CDV-Hvac).
source: There were five potential glycosylation sites (Asn149, Asn391, Asn422, Asn456, and Asn587) in the H protein head domain of the Kyoto Biken vaccine strain (CDV-Hvac) and two additional sites (Asn309 and Asn603) in the 5VD wild-type strain (CDV-Hwt) (Figure 6A).

claim: There were two additional glycosylation sites (Asn309 and Asn603) in the 5VD wild-type strain (CDV-Hwt).
source: There were five potential glycosylation sites (Asn149, Asn391, Asn422, Asn456, and Asn587) in the H protein head domain of the Kyoto Biken vaccine strain (CDV-Hvac) and two additional sites (Asn309 and Asn603) in the 5VD wild-type strain (CDV-Hwt) (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Western blot analysis indicated that all asparagine CDV-H mutants except for the N309D and N603D mutants migrated further than the wild-type, revealing that both CDV-Hvac and CDV-H wt have five sugar chains in common glycosylation sites (Asn149, Asn391, Asn422, Asn456, and Asn587).
source: Western blot analysis indicated that all asparagine CDV-H mutants except for the N309D and N603D mutants migrated further than the wild-type, revealing that both CDV-Hvac and CDV-H wt have five sugar chains in common glycosylation sites (Asn149, Asn391, Asn422, Asn456, and Asn587) (Figure 6B), while Asn309 and Asn603 specific to CDV-Hwt are not glycosylated.

claim: Asn309 and Asn603 specific to CDV-Hwt are not glycosylated.
source: Western blot analysis indicated that all asparagine CDV-H mutants except for the N309D and N603D mutants migrated further than the wild-type, revealing that both CDV-Hvac and CDV-H wt have five sugar chains in common glycosylation sites (Asn149, Asn391, Asn422, Asn456, and Asn587) (Figure 6B), while Asn309 and Asn603 specific to CDV-Hwt are not glycosylated.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: This result is consistent with a previous report showing that five standard glycosylation sites exist in the ectodomain of the wild-type CDV-H protein.
source: This result is consistent with a previous report showing that five standard glycosylation sites exist in the ectodomain of the wild-type CDV-H protein (Sawatsky and von Messling, 2010).

claim: The CDV-H structure, which contains five N-linked sugars, exhibits electron density only for Asn422-linked GlcNAc.
source: The CDV-H structure, which contains five N-linked sugars as described above, exhibits electron density only for Asn422-linked GlcNAc (Figure 2D).

claim: Asn149- and Asn422-linked sugars, which are located close to each other, appear to bury internal spaces between the stalk and head domains.
source: Asn149- and Asn422-linked sugars, which are located close to each other, appear to bury internal spaces between the stalk and head domains, and Asn587-linked sugars might support the stabilization of the CDV-H dimer orientation (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).

claim: Asn587-linked sugars might support the stabilization of the CDV-H dimer orientation.
source: Asn149- and Asn422-linked sugars, which are located close to each other, appear to bury internal spaces between the stalk and head domains, and Asn587-linked sugars might support the stabilization of the CDV-H dimer orientation (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section as a speculation and shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Sugars modified on Asn391, Asn456, and Asn587 seemed to cover the large pocket in CDV-H.
source: Sugars modified on Asn391, Asn456, and Asn587 seemed to cover the large pocket in CDV-H, and Asn456-linked sugars appeared to lean toward the center of the pocket (Figure 6C).

claim: The majority of CDV-H surfaces are covered with sugars, forcing only the RBSs to be exposed.

claim: The crystal structure of CDV-H shows a connector domain (residues 158–187) that mediates a head domain to the stalk region, which facilitates head-to-head homodimer formation with a set of disulfide bonds at Cys154.
source: The crystal structure of CDV-H shows a connector domain (residues 158–187) that mediates a head domain to the stalk region, which facilitates head-to-head homodimer formation with a set of disulfide bonds at Cys154 (Figures 1A and 7A).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and shown in Figures 1A and 7A.

claim: There were no covalent bonds in the homodimer interface of the head domains.
source: Interestingly, there were no covalent bonds in the homodimer interface of the head domains, even though a conserved homodimer orientation was observed in the crystal structures of CDV-H and MeV-H, as described above.

claim: Each head domain of CDV-H also dissociates and moves flexibly, as shown in the structure of Nipah virus (NiV)-G protein.
source: This observation raises the possibility that each head domain of CDV-H also dissociates and moves flexibly, as shown in the structure of Nipah virus (NiV)-G protein, previously (Wang et al., 2022).

claim: The CDV-H dimer was observed as two globules clustered together in most cases, but sometimes, each domain moved independently.

evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and shown in Figure 7B and Videos 1–3.

claim: CDV-H could adopt both associated and dissociated forms.
source: Time-course analysis of the dynamics of the representative CDV-H dimer showed that CDV-H could adopt both associated and dissociated forms (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The distribution of distances between each head domain in the CDV-H dimers showed approximately 15 nm as a major peak.
source: Finally, the distribution of distances between each head domain in the CDV-H dimers showed approximately 15 nm as a major peak (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and shown in Figure 7D.

claim: 15 nm is a reasonable length for the linker between the head domain dimers.
source: This is a reasonable length for the linker between the head domain dimers.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section as an interpretation of the distance measurement.

source: The overall structure of the head domain shows a folding similar to that of MeV-H (Hashiguchi et al., 2007) and a homodimer with a tilted domain orientation is formed, essentially the same as the MeV-H homodimer, which is consistent with the cryo-EM structure of wild-type CDV-H ectodomain (Kalbermatter et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: The binding of CDV-H to dNectin-4 was demonstrated by SPR, revealing low-affinity and fast-kinetic interactions, similar to SLAM binding.
source: The binding of CDV-H to dNectin-4 was demonstrated by SPR, revealing low-affinity and fast-kinetic interactions, similar to SLAM binding.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion section summarizing the SPR results.

claim: Low-affinity and fast-kinetics interactions between viral attachment proteins and their receptors on target cells do not cause significant structural changes.
source: The conventional idea that low-affinity and fast-kinetics interactions between viral attachment proteins and their receptors on target cells do not cause significant structural changes (Dimitrov, 2004), suggesting that CDV-H-receptor recognition is essentially similar to that of MeV.
